about: Agencies filed under two IDs (ORIs) in the Crime Index files. Read by the engine (lib/nibrs-shadow/ori-crosswalk.ts) and copied as-is into the blind checker's folder, so both count each agency once under the ID in `same_as`, which is the ID the place index (scripts/fixtures/nibrs-shadow/agencies.json) gives the agency, so a lookup by that ID finds every year. `files` says which file the pair applies to. In `current` (AH Datalytics' Final file, current_final, and crimeindex.org's current_crime download), every row of `id` is read as `same_as`. In `historical_crime` (agency_crime), each ID owns the years in `owns`: a year's row is kept only from the ID that owns that year, then read as `same_as`, so each agency has exactly one row per year. Each pair has its evidence. Add a pair only with the same evidence: no year with counts under both IDs, the ranges meet, and the population carries on across the change. Found by scanning crimeindex-20261119 (nibrsai-review/historical-two-id-agencies-20261122.md); the same-name pairs that are two agencies, the sheriff-and-county-police pairs and the pairs far apart in years are deliberately left out.

pairs.evidence: Final file: MI631900X, 2017-01 to 2026-09 (117 months). current_crime: MI6367300, 2025-01 to 2026-09 (21 months, sample true). The seven Part I counts are equal in all 21 shared months (2025-01: 49 violent crimes in both). Neither ID is in the other file. Listed as a known difference in nibrs-model docs/RUNBOOK.md.

Counts under MI631900X 1930-1959 and 2025, under MI6367300 1960-2010; 2011-2024 have no counts under either ID (rows with a population only), so they stay blank. No year has counts under both. Population 1959 81,378 (MI631900X), 1960 82,233 (MI6367300).
Counts under MO0360600 1961-2001, MO0281000 2002-2025; no shared year. Population 2001 6,390, 2002 6,439.
